findings.title: Live polling synchronously materializes and reparses up to 64 MiB
findings.where: src/lib/live-session.ts:36 defaults the cap to 67,108,864 bytes; src/lib/live-session.ts:98-121 synchronously copies chunks and concatenates them; src/lib/live-session.ts:319-340 then scans and parses the complete merged string multiple times.
findings.what: Each live-session invocation can block the server while reading up to 64 MiB, retain chunk buffers plus concatenated Buffer/string copies, scan it for newest timestamps, and parse it again for token and tool views. The cap prevents unbounded growth but still permits substantial per-poll latency and transient memory, and this surface has no latency/memory probe or budget.
findings.fix: Use a bounded tail/incremental transcript reader and share one parsed event pass across liveness, token, and tool derivation; add an explicit live-poll latency and peak-memory budget at the maximum supported transcript size.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark/probe using a 64 MiB transcript demonstrates the live-session request stays within the documented latency and memory budgets, and instrumentation or tests show transcript bytes are not synchronously materialized and fully parsed multiple times per poll.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the default 64 MiB cap, synchronous read/copy/concatenation, and three distinct full-content consumers on the same invocation. The cap and single-candidate selection mitigate scope but do not remove the per-request stall and allocation hotspot.

findings.title: Scripted evaluation results can be mislabeled as live-model receipts
findings.where: src/lib/local-analyze-eval.ts:133-145 exposes endpoint and endpointKind as independent caller-controlled options; src/lib/local-analyze-eval.ts:227-238 stamps endpointKind without verifying the transport; src/lib/local-analyze-eval.test.ts:137-155 passes scriptedAnalyzeEndpoint with endpointKind='live' and expects live provenance.
findings.what: The structured provenance field intended to distinguish synthetic fixtures from real local-model evidence is not tied to the transport that produced the measurement. A caller can run the scripted fixture endpoint, label the record live, and publish synthetic pass rates as real calibration evidence.
findings.fix: Make provenance intrinsic to the endpoint abstraction, such as separate scripted/live runner functions or a branded endpoint object whose immutable kind is used by runAnalyzeEval; remove the independent endpointKind override.
findings.acceptance: No public API can pair scriptedAnalyzeEndpoint with live provenance, and a regression test proves scripted executions always emit endpointKind='scripted' while only a constructed live transport can emit 'live'.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read both implementation and test. The mismatch is directly reproducible from the audited API, and the test explicitly validates the false scripted-as-live pairing rather than preventing it.
